title: Did the TRIIM trial reverse epigenetic aging in humans?
question: The TRIIM study reported that epigenetic age was reversed in humans. Identify the design, who was enrolled and analyzed, what was given, what the epigenetic-age result was compared against, and whether reversal of biological aging is established.
verdict_question: Did TRIIM establish that the treatment reversed biological aging in humans?

source.title: Reversal of epigenetic aging and immunosenescent trends in humans
source.license: CC BY 4.0; verify before reusing text

fields: epigenetic age result and its comparator
whether a reversal of biological aging is established
acceptance_criteria: State whether there was a concurrent control group, and what any 'compared to no treatment' figure is compared against
Distinguish participants recruited from participants analyzed
Name every component of the combined intervention; do not attribute effects to one drug
Distinguish the thymus objective from the epigenetic-clock results
Do not equate a clock-predicted lifespan gain with measured lifespan
result_destination: Submit to https://longevidence.org/challenge/api/submit (see join.txt). Public, marked unreviewed.
publication_acceptance: submissions are public drafts; not reviewed or accepted until marked by a reviewer
